<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by keeping the duty’s actual boundary live: after the swatting kit is gone, PRO still treats “throwaway brigades” and coordination layers as suppressible vectors that anonymous lawful organizing also uses. PRO’s gap/externality case was strong and CON conceded platforms should strip addresses and fake-emergency scripts, but CON showed that a foreseeability duty plus a one-way shield still makes disabling mixed campaigns the safer legal bet, and that the clear crime does not justify the broader obligation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A4 vs B4 on the express shield: PRO claimed shielding leftover organizing breaks the chilling asymmetry; CON showed platforms must still defend a disputed “brigade vs. campaign” classification after injury, so overblocking remains safer.</best_rebuttal>
